findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "beleeg_start_league" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Creates a real league on Beleeg right away for someone who does not have a Beleeg account yet: the league, its first season with registration open, optional tea…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "beleeg_start_league" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "public" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: beleeg_start_league, beleeg_start_tournament · Public sink: beleeg_start_league, beleeg_start_tournament, beleeg_send_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: beleeg_start_league, beleeg_start_tournament · Public sink: beleeg_start_league, beleeg_start_tournament, beleeg_send_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
